deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a sheet of magnetometer observations from Gauss's induction experiments with Weber (1830s): 'Phys. 4', 22 March, air temperature 6.8 °C. It continues the series on the neighbouring pages (24 March: P.O., P.U., 'Ohne M.').

Each series lists 12 scale readings a_0,...,a_11, taken at successive elongations (turning points) of the needle. The deviations from the mean decrease roughly linearly, pass through zero and grow again with the opposite phase (for I, about 364, 295, 227, 162, 95, 30, then -34, -97, ...). This is the signature of a deflecting force that is reversed at every turning point (multiplication / recoil method). Under that interpretation the equilibrium point alternates between e1, for the pairs (a_{2k}, a_{2k+1}), and e2, for the pairs (a_{2k+1}, a_{2k+2}). The quantity sought is 2(e2 - e1), the double deflection in scale divisions.

Step 1 (pair sums and differences). For each pair Gauss writes the sum and the difference.
- Column A: S_k = a_{2k} + a_{2k+1} and D_k = a_{2k+1} - a_{2k}, for k = 0..5.
- Column B: S'_k = a_{2k+1} + a_{2k+2} and D'_k = a_{2k+2} - a_{2k+1}, for k = 0..4.
- Series I, A: 1886.9+658.7, 1890.9+389.3, 1891.2+125.6, 1892.9-130.7, 1893.4-383.0, 1893.6-629.2.
- Series I, B: 2023.6-522.0, 2022.9-257.3, 2020.2+3.4, 2019.3+257.1, 2016.6+506.2.

Step 2 (damping model; my explanation of why the sum drifts with the difference). Take a damped swing about equilibrium e with ratio lambda between successive amplitudes, so that a_k - e = A and a_{k+1} - e = -lambda*A. Then
- a_k + a_{k+1} = 2e + (1 - lambda)A,
- a_{k+1} - a_k = -(1 + lambda)A,
- hence 2e = S + x*D, with x = (1 - lambda)/(1 + lambda).
So each pair gives 2e1 = S_k + x*D_k, or 2e2 = S'_k + x*D'_k. Averaging gives:
- 2e1 = mean(S) + x*mean(D) = 1891.483 + 5.1x (since 11348.9/6 = 1891.483 and 30.7/6 = 5.12);
- 2e2 = 2020.520 - 2.5x (since 10102.6/5 = 2020.52 and -12.6/5 = -2.52).

Step 3 (difference of the two equilibria). 2(e2 - e1) = 129.037 - 7.6x.

Step 4 (estimating x empirically from the data). Over the run, the sums change by:
- column A: 1893.6 - 1886.9 = 6.7, while the differences span 658.7 + 629.2 = 1287.9;
- column B: 2023.6 - 2016.6 = 7.0, while the differences span 522.0 + 506.2 = 1028.2.
Pooling the two columns: x = 13.7/2316.1 = 1/169. This corresponds to lambda ≈ 0.988.

Step 5 (result for I). The correction is 7.6/169 = 0.045, so 2(e2 - e1) = 129.037 - 0.045 = 128.992.

Series II (Temp 6.8 °C), same procedure:
- Column A: 1885.0+631.6, 1885.9+361.7, 1887.2+99.0, 1888.5-157.1, 1889.8-407.8, 1889.1-652.9; means 1887.583 - 20.9x.
- Column B: 2020.4-496.2, 2017.9-229.7, 2015.9+29.7, 2014.5+283.1, 2012.0+530.0; means 2016.140 + 23.4x.
- Difference: 128.557 + 44.3x.
- Estimate of x: (4.1 + 8.4)/(1284.5 + 1026.2) = 12.5/2310.7 = 1/184.9.
- Correction: 44.3/184.9 = 0.239.
- Result: 128.796.

Series III (9 readings) is struck through, with reading 7 corrected to 672.0. It is evidently abandoned; the next page restarts III.

For comparison, the 24 March sheet gives 130.554, 126.447 and 128.587 for its three configurations.
errors: No arithmetic errors found once the image is read correctly. All sums, differences, means, the x estimates and the final corrections check.

Methodological remark rather than an error: x is estimated crudely from the end-to-end change of the sums against the end-to-end span of the differences. It is not a least-squares fit of S on D, but it is adequate for a correction of only 0.04-0.24 divisions.

The model 2e = S + x*D assumes a geometric damping ratio that is the same for both half-swings. The pooled x averages two noticeably different column estimates (1/192 and 1/147 in I), which shows the noise in this damping estimate.

results.what: Equilibrium positions from successive elongation pairs, with a damping correction 2e = a_k + a_{k+1} + x(a_{k+1} - a_k), x = (1 - lambda)/(1 + lambda)
results.modern_name: Damping-corrected determination of the rest position of a damped oscillator from turning points

results.what: Deflection measured by reversing the deflecting force at each elongation (alternating equilibria e1, e2; amplitude changes linearly), evaluated as 2(e2 - e1)
results.modern_name: Multiplication method / method of recoil (Zurückwerfungsmethode) for galvanometers and inductors
results.usually_credited_to: W. Weber and Gauss, Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins, c. 1837-1838

results.what: Empirical estimate of the damping coefficient x from the drift of pair sums against pair differences (x = 1/169 and 1/184.9)
results.modern_name: Estimation of the logarithmic decrement from observed elongations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine laboratory reduction sheet from the Gauss-Weber induction and magnetometer work. It applies their known reduction technique (pair sums with a damping correction, alternating equilibria from the multiplication/recoil method). No new mathematics is involved.
